title: Cherry clafoutis
summary: Sweet cherries baked in a puffed, custardy almond batter, served warm with a dusting of powdered sweetener.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C (350 °F). Butter a 23 cm (9 in) pie dish or shallow baking dish and spread the cherries over the base.
Whisk the eggs and erythritol until frothy, then whisk in the almond flour and salt until smooth.
Whisk in the cream, almond milk, vanilla and almond extract. The batter will be thin, like a crêpe batter.
Pour the batter gently over the cherries.
Bake 35–40 minutes, until puffed, golden at the edges and just set in the centre; a knife inserted midway should come out clean.
Cool 15 minutes; it sinks as it cools, which is normal. Dust with powdered erythritol and serve warm.
dairy_free_notes: With coconut cream the custard is slightly denser and has a mild coconut note; the almond extract helps cover it.
tips: In Limousin the cherries are traditionally left unpitted, which adds a faint almond flavour from the stones; warn your guests if you do this.
Cherries are high in sugar for a fruit, so keep to the weight given.

origin.history: Clafoutis is a country dessert from the Limousin region of central France, made by pouring a thick pancake-like batter over black cherries and baking it. It spread to the rest of France in the nineteenth century. Strictly, only the cherry version is called clafoutis; made with other fruit, the French usually call it a flaugnarde.
